topic: Closed-form sharp binary frontier under longitudinal product sensitivity ratios. Observe positive binary O=(A0,A1,L1,Y) with degenerate baseline, target mu11=E[Y(1,1)], fixed interior margin eta, and Tan product ratios lambda1, lambda0L, lambda0Y bounded by finite G,B,C. Impose exactly Tan Lemma 7's cellwise normalization constraints and use Lemma 8's compatible-law objective. Prove both sharp endpoints are attained and equal explicit evaluations of at most 64 rational branches each after reducing the ratios to binary success probabilities and one L1 reweighting. Prove complete necessary-and-sufficient observable conditions for equality versus strictness of both Proposition-3 conservative endpoints, including sensitivity-free faces and active ties. Construct multinomial plug-in confidence sets with uniform asymptotic coverage for the entire sharp interval over the eta-interior class using an all-branch Gaussian-multiplier envelope. Credit Tan (Biometrika 2025) for the product model, exact compatibility, generic sharp optimization, conservative bounds, and sensitivity-free exact faces; credit Bonvini et al. for longitudinal MSM sensitivity. Dickerman et al.'s repeated-strategy metformin target-trial analysis is the consumer for the absolute sustained-metformin cancer risk; no contrast or sign-breakdown claim is made. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: All ten ratio cells reduce to r_l=e_l p_l+(1-e_l)U_G(p_l), t_l=U_B(r_l), and one endpoint L1 reweighting, yielding at most 64 rational branches and attaining full-data laws. The supplied witness reproduces [0.3625,0.6375]. For active covariate sensitivity Tan v1 is strictly loose; for G,B>1 v2 is exact iff (p_l-1/(G+1))(r_l-1/(B+1))>=0 in both strata, with ties included. A strict interior witness gives sharp 61/80, v1 25/32, and v2 49/64; 1,000 random exact comparisons found no criterion failure. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform Gaussian-multiplier quantile approximation over all branch gradients, including redundant or zero-variance coordinates, and the uniform quadratic remainder bound across branch changes; independently verify both equality-chain proofs against the final published Proposition 3. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the published binary check-loss programs and certify the rational strictness witness 61/80 versus 25/32 and 49/64; a different shared-threshold specification requires re-deriving the strictness theorem before proceeding. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_productratio_binary_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For the positive binary two-decision product-ratio model, reduce Tan's Lemma 8 compatible-law programs to explicit lower and upper endpoints given by at most 64 rational branches and prove that every endpoint is attained by a compatible full-data law.

source_refs.claim: Lemma 8 gives a sharp product-model bound through constrained optimization over sensitivity ratios satisfying the Lemma 7 normalization constraints, while ratio coupling obstructs a general exact unconstrained representation.
source_refs.author: Zhiqiang Tan

source_refs.claim: Quantile balancing produces the narrowest cross-sectional marginal-sensitivity interval and constructs extremal normalized weights, providing the closest threshold-reduction analogue.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn and Kevin Guo
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Enumerate clipping faces on finite support and give exact algebraic primal-dual certificates, including inactive prices.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tan supplies exact compatibility constraints and a sharp constrained program, but the intermediate-covariate and outcome sensitivity ratios remain coupled. Binary support may collapse the optimization to finitely many threshold or extreme-point cases, as suggested by the prior finite-support face-enumeration direction, but completeness still requires assigning every feasible optimizer to a branch, handling denominators and tied thresholds throughout the positive interior, and lifting every optimizing ratio tuple through Lemma 7 to an attaining full-data law. The targeted literature scan found no such binary product-model reduction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp partial-identification theorem expressing both endpoints as extrema of at most 64 explicitly specified rational functions of the observed cell probabilities and (G,B,C), with an exhaustive branch partition and a compatible-law construction attaining each selected endpoint.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from sequential non-confounding through ratio restrictions and observable compatibility to sharp and conservative population bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sequential exchangeability is untestable -> bounded longitudinal density ratios define a sensitivity model -> exact compatibility yields a sharp but implicit optimization -> binary support may expose a closed-form finite frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the necessity-and-sufficiency normalization proof of Lemma 7 and the compatible-law reassembly behind Lemma 8 after parameterizing each binary ratio by a success probability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It defines exactly the feasible full-data-law fiber whose binary extreme points must be enumerated and whose endpoint attainment must be certified.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the quantile-balancing and complementary-slackness proof that normalized bounded density-ratio programs attain extrema at threshold weights, replacing the single-period threshold with coupled binary cell thresholds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems seek a sharp observed-law formula and an attaining confounding law under bounded likelihood ratios; the product model adds sequential compatibility coupling.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt efficient endpoint linearization and multiplier simultaneous-band construction to the finite family of smooth rational branch estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the frontier is finite, each branch has a plug-in influence-function expansion, with nonsmooth branch selection as the additional inference step.

open_problems.open_problem: Give complete observable necessary-and-sufficient conditions for equality, active ties, and strictness between each sharp binary product-model endpoint and Tan's Proposition 3 v1 and v2 conservative endpoints, including every sensitivity-free face.

source_refs.claim: Proposition 3 supplies two generally conservative bounds, while Corollary 1 establishes exactness only on restricted sensitivity-free cases.
source_refs.author: Zhiqiang Tan

source_refs.claim: Dropping an inherent normalization or balancing constraint can leave marginal-sensitivity bounds asymptotically wider than the sharp compatible interval.
source_refs.author: Jacob Dorn and Kevin Guo
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: The strict open-set gap demonstrates that common-law compatibility has empirical content

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tan proves general conservativeness and identifies selected exact sensitivity-free faces, but does not give a complete binary iff frontier. Such a frontier must reverse every relaxation, monotonicity, and convexity step in the published Proposition 3 proof and translate equality into observable cell-probability conditions, including cases where a check-loss threshold ties a binary cell or a sensitivity component equals one. The prior common-law proposal shows that omitted compatibility can create a strict open-set gap, but its shared-confounder geometry does not establish the equality conditions for Tan's sequential product normalizations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Endpoint-specific if-and-only-if theorems partitioning the observable eta-interior parameter space into equality and strictness regions for Proposition 3 v1 and v2 using explicit weak inequalities with ties included, together with exact treatment of all sensitivity-free faces and rational witnesses for nonempty strict regions.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its sharp-versus-conservative comparison and special exact faces as the starting point, presenting the new result as completion of the binary equality frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The product model has exact compatibility constraints -> tractable relaxations yield conservative Proposition 3 endpoints -> restricted sensitivity-free faces are known to be exact -> binary observables may permit a complete equality-versus-strictness characterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Reverse the published Proposition 3 inequality chains and impose equality in every monotonicity, convexity, and conditional-expectation step before specializing the conditions to binary cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result asks exactly when Tan's two tractable bounding constructions coincide with the Lemma 8 sharp value.

method_exemplars.technique: Use quantile-balancing complementary slackness to characterize when an optimizer of a relaxed bounded-weight problem also satisfies the omitted normalization constraint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The structural analogy is that looseness arises when a relaxed likelihood-ratio optimizer violates compatibility-implied balance.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt optimized-value influence functions and the distinction between sharp and merely valid endpoint inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The equality frontier determines where a conservative endpoint estimates the sharp endpoint and where inference must preserve their nonzero gap.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an all-branch Gaussian-multiplier confidence set with uniform asymptotic coverage for the entire sharp binary product-sensitivity interval over an eta-interior multinomial class, allowing active ties, redundant branches, singular covariance, and zero-variance branch-gradient coordinates.

source_refs.claim: Tan's population analysis leaves sample estimation and inference for the sequential product sensitivity model as future work.
source_refs.author: Zhiqiang Tan

source_refs.claim: For other longitudinal sensitivity models, the authors develop efficient estimators and confidence intervals for causal-parameter bounds under time-varying treatment.
source_refs.author: Matteo Bonvini, Edward H. Kennedy, Valerie Ventura, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: The ordinary bootstrap generally fails for directionally differentiable but non-differentiable maps; derivative-aware resampling restores validity under appropriate conditions.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Gaussian and Gaussian-multiplier approximations are established for coordinatewise maxima without restrictions on cross-coordinate correlations.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

uniform inference at the branch switches and degeneracies emphasized by the tipping atlas remains open.
Uniform tangent inference through zero cells, optimizer ties, and moving odds faces remains an explicit open problem.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A finite branch representation remains nonregular at active ties because each endpoint is a min or max of smooth rational maps. Redundant branches, identical gradients, and zero-variance coordinates can make the Gaussian covariance singular. Fang and Santos explain why an ordinary plug-in bootstrap is unreliable at nondifferentiable points, while CCK-style multiplier theory addresses correlated maxima but does not by itself supply the uniform branchwise quadratic remainder or the causal-interval coverage argument. Prior CausalSmith runs independently left uniform inference at branch switches, zero cells, and moving faces unresolved, and Bonvini et al.'s inference applies to a different longitudinal sensitivity model.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem proving that a multinomial plug-in interval enlarged by the conditional quantile of the maximum over all lower- and upper-branch multiplier gradients covers the complete sharp identified interval uniformly at level 1-alpha over the eta-interior class, with a uniform quadratic remainder and validity under ties and singular covariance.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from closed-form sharp sensitivity bounds to efficient endpoint estimation and simultaneous multiplier bands, while foregrounding the new finite-branch nonregularity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp sensitivity bounds are population objects -> closed-form branches permit influence-function expansions -> applications need uncertainty for the whole identified interval -> an all-branch multiplier envelope may deliver uniform coverage if ties and degeneracy are controlled.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Gaussian comparison, anti-concentration, and conditional Gaussian-multiplier approximation to the fixed vector of all branch influence functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed critical value is a maximum of correlated branch-gradient sums, and retaining every branch avoids estimating a discontinuous active set.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the directional delta method for finite min/max maps and derivative-aware resampling along local sequences approaching active branch ties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoints are finite extrema of smooth rational maps, the canonical directionally differentiable functionals for which ordinary bootstrap consistency can fail at ties.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt uniform inference for optimized value functions, including bootstrap approximation of directional derivatives and uniform one-sided size control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A sharp bound is an optimized value functional, and the requested result requires uniform rather than pointwise coverage across branch changes.

literature_map:
Tan (2025, Biometrika, arXiv:2308.15725) is the direct anchor: Lemmas 7–8 encode exact product-model compatibility and sharp optimization, Proposition 3 gives two generally conservative relaxations, and the paper leaves sample inference open.
Tan's product model separately bounds counterfactual-covariate and outcome ratios; their coupling is the stated obstacle to a general exact unconstrained representation.
Bonvini, Kennedy, Ventura, and Wasserman (2022, arXiv:2210.04681) treat time-varying marginal-sensitivity models and provide efficient estimators and confidence intervals, but under restrictions different from Tan's exact product compatibility.
Brumback, Hernán, Haneuse, and Robins (2004, Statistics in Medicine, DOI 10.1002/sim.1657) provide an older repeated-measures MSM sensitivity anchor using specified confounding-bias functions rather than sharp bounded-ratio compatibility.
Robins, Rotnitzky, and Scharfstein (2000, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4612-1284-3_1) anchor selection-odds sensitivity for longitudinal missingness and unmeasured confounding.
Tan (2006, JASA, DOI 10.1198/016214506000000023) supplies a cross-sectional distributional and propensity-score origin for marginal sensitivity models.
Zhao, Small, and Bhattacharya (2019, JRSSB, arXiv:1711.11286) derive percentile-bootstrap intervals through linear-fractional programming, while later sharpness work shows why relaxed bounds may remain too wide.
Dorn and Guo (2023, JASA, arXiv:2102.04543) use quantile balancing to derive sharp cross-sectional MSM bounds and the narrowest compatible interval, furnishing the closest finite-threshold identification analogy.
Dorn, Guo, and Kallus (2024, JASA, arXiv:2112.11449) develop doubly sharp and doubly valid estimation, semiparametric efficiency, and Wald inference for cross-sectional sharp sensitivity bounds.
Zhang and Zhao (arXiv:2211.04697) derive closed-form sharp average-case sensitivity bounds, efficient endpoint estimators, and multiplier simultaneous bands under a different sensitivity model.
Fang and Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:1404.3763) show the generic bootstrap failure for non-differentiable directional maps and develop derivative-aware resampling.
Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1911.10215) develop uniform bootstrap inference for optimized value functions using directional differentiability.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1212.6906) provide Gaussian-multiplier approximation for maxima with unrestricted cross-coordinate correlation.
Dickerman et al. (2023, Epidemiology, DOI 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001626) estimate six-year cancer risks under metformin target-trial strategies, making absolute sustained-strategy risk a concrete consumer of a longitudinal sharp interval.
The targeted scan found no paper deriving a finite closed-form binary product-ratio frontier, a complete Proposition 3 equality/strictness characterization, or uniform all-branch inference with ties and zero-variance coordinates.
